sources.title: FY2025 results
sources.supports: annual sales, BOI and free cash flow

sources.title: Riliprubart trial report
sources.supports: contextual negative only; paywalled and excluded from decisive conclusion

financial_anchor.caveat: Adjusted non-IFRS BOI; 2026 growth is affected by acquisitions and FX.

ai_claim.claim: Sanofi has production-oriented AI discovery and trial-recruitment programmes, including two partner-reported discovery milestones and Muse.
ai_claim.scope: Two discovery programmes and an announced recruitment tool, not the portfolio
ai_claim.limitation: No matched prospective transition-rate, enrollment-quality or retained-cash result.

strongest_counterevidence.claim: Public AI programme disclosures do not provide prospective matched clinical-transition or retained-cash results; a reported riliprubart futility stop is contextual only.
strongest_counterevidence.limitation: Paywalled and primary release inaccessible; programme not identified as AI-designed, so excluded from decisive causal evidence.

rights_limit: Trial data are consent/protocol constrained; public contracts do not establish pooled cross-trial or cross-customer training rights.
materiality_summary: Five percent of FY2025 BOI is €607m per year. The separate stage-adjusted portfolio calculation is a one-time present value and cannot establish annual hurdle clearance without cohort timing and annuitization.

arithmetic.inputs: Annual hurdle: €12,149m×5%. Separate PV illustration: 20 entries; €250m stage-adjusted value each; 15% lift; 80% capture; recurring platform cost €100m/year
arithmetic.result: €607m/year hurdle; €600m one-time portfolio PV before recurring cost; incomparable bases, so no break-even claim

g2_provisional: Insufficient: E2 workflow evidence exists, but no prospective quality-adjusted clinical productivity result.
unresolved_questions: What is Muse's matched production result and net cost?
